title: Priority Fabric for Advisory Requests with Customer Value Encoder
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a prioritized intake pipeline ("priority fabric") for non-bug optimization and advisory requests (batching/caching knobs, quantization profiles, routing policies). The pipeline will encode customer value signals — SLA sensitivity, monthly spend, churn risk, compliance requirements, and engineering effort estimate — into a single score used to route requests into lanes: self-serve docs, concierge advisory, or eng-backed delivery (Dedicated/Private work). Goal: reduce time-to-first-response for high-value customers, prevent engineer triage thrash, and standardize handoffs with measurable SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Priority encoder computes a stable score for incoming requests; scoring model reproducible and documented
A2: Precision@top-10 for high-priority routing >= 0.85 on holdout historical triage labels
A3: Routing rules implemented in intake service and tested end-to-end (self-serve / concierge / eng-delivery lanes)
A4: Console shows per-lane backlog, expected SLA, and per-request score in UI
A5: Hand-off playbook created with templates for concierge and eng-delivery tickets; 80% of concierge handoffs follow template
A6: Metrics: median time-to-first-response for high-priority requests reduced by >= 40% in pilot
design_notes: Design to include compact score badge (0-100) visible on intake card, hover reveals contributing signals. Keep self-serve lane friction minimal: if score below threshold, surface targeted KB articles and a short form. Work with Design (Priya Singh) to prototype two UX variations for pilot.
engineering_notes: Prototype scorer as LightGBM model trained on past 24 months of labeled triage outcomes + engineered signals (monthly-spend, SLA-flag, churn-score, infra-type, customer-size, previous-advisories). Fallback deterministic rules if model unavailable. Intake service to expose score via /intake API and event to ingestion topic. Require feature flags for gradual rollout.
progress_updates: 2026-02-25: Discovery complete — 7 enterprise customers interviewed (notes in doc). Key signal takeaways: cost-sensitivity and SLA tier are top routing factors; customers willing to accept longer delivery if cost savings >= 25%
2026-03-03: Data pull ready — labeled ~4.2k historical advisory tickets; feature engineering pipeline (snowplow -> parquet) validated
2026-03-05: Prototype scorer trained (LightGBM). Cross-val shows Precision@top-10 = 0.82, Recall@top-10 = 0.47. Need to tune features and thresholding to meet acceptance criteria
2026-03-08: Design review scheduled 2026-03-15 with Priya; shortlist two UI patterns for score badge and automated suggestion flows
2026-03-10: Eng spike completed for intake API and feature flagging. Created stub endpoints and test harness. Integration with console telemetry agreed (endpoint /intake/v1/score).
2026-03-12: Product decision: run 4-week concierge pilot for customers with score >= 65 and monthly spend >= $10k. Pilot cohort list compiled (see artifacts).
tradeoffs_and_open_questions: Q1: Model vs rules — prefer model for signal fusion but deterministic fallback needed for explainability and auditability
Q2: Score transparency — how much to reveal to customers? Proposal: reveal score band (Low/Medium/High) and contributing top-3 signals, but not raw score formula
Q3: SLA obligations — routing to concierge implies a soft SLA (2 business days); routing to eng-delivery may require contract amendment for Dedicated/Private customers
Q4: Cost to run scorer in real-time vs batch — initial plan: score at intake (sync) with caching; heavy re-score only on signal-change events
